description: The correctness of cross-operation role uniqueness in a single Mailbox/set request depends on maintaining two semantically distinct sets: (1) what this request intends to free (scanned from update patches before execution), and (2) what actually freed (built only from updates that succeeded). A failed vacate must not release the role, so a subsequent create claiming that role in the same request must be rejected. The old names (roles_vacated_by_updates / roles_actually_vacated) blurred this intent-vs-outcome distinction — 'actually_vacated' reads as a synonym for 'vacated_by_updates' rather than as the post-execution ground truth. The new names make the two-phase protocol explicit. A contributor might suggest merging them into one set or shortening to roles_freed / roles_vacated, which would silently lose the distinction and re-introduce the bug the two-set design prevents.
title: roles_intended_to_vacate vs roles_successfully_vacated names encode load-bearing semantic distinction
